targets.authors: Boor K, Van Der Vleuten C, Teunissen P, Scherpbier A, Scheele F
targets.title: Development and analysis of D-RECT, an instrument measuring residents' learning climate
targets.evidence_quote:
Aim:  Boor et al [ 1 ] developed and validated the questionnaire D-RECT (Dutch Residency Educational Climate Test ) to measure the clinical learning environment within the medical specialist training. In this study, a German version of this questionnaire (D-RECT German) is analyzed regarding testtheoretical properties.
Problem:  Are the results of Boor et al replicable as a proof for validity of the questionnaire D-RECT?
targets.outcome_quote: Confirmatory factor analysis uncovered fundamental weaknesses in the eleven-factorial model of Boor et al. Analysis of loading weight as well as intercorrelation of the subscales point towards a different underlying structure of the D-RECT-German compared with the original instrument.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central factorial structure and validity test fails: authors say the eleven-factor model has fundamental weaknesses and insufficient evidence of international validity. Counts of individual subscale reliability differences do not establish mixed replication of that central finding.

reasoning: New German sample explicitly tests whether the original D-RECT psychometric findings replicate, rather than only applying a questionnaire descriptively. Other validation papers are discussed as context, not independently re-tested.
